rationale: The clause states that risk categorisation is reviewed at the time of periodic updation but fails to specify the mandatory risk-based periodicity (2 years for high-risk, 8 years for medium-risk, and 10 years for low-risk customers) required by the RBI Directions.

evidence.quote: The bank shall carry out periodic updation at least once in every two years for high-risk customers, once in every eight years for medium risk customers and once in every 10 years for low-risk customers from the date of opening of the account / last KYC updation.

arguments.query: The risk categorisation of customer accounts shall be reviewed at the time of periodic updation of KYC.

rationale: The clause accurately reflects the minimum periodicity requirements for periodic KYC updation for high, medium, and low-risk customers as mandated by the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025.

evidence.quote: However, the bank shall carry out periodic updation at least once in every two years for high-risk customers, once in every eight years for medium risk customers and once in every 10 years for low-risk customers from the date of opening of the account / last KYC updation.

arguments.query: Periodic updation of KYC shall be carried out at least once every two years for high-risk customers, once every eight years for medium-risk customers and once every ten years for low-risk customers, from the date of opening of the account or the last KYC updation.

rationale: The clause mandates three advance intimations but omits the specific requirement that at least one of these intimations must be sent by letter, as mandated by the RBI Directions.

evidence.quote: Prior to the due date of periodic updation of KYC, the bank shall give at least three advance intimations, including at least one intimation by letter, at appropriate intervals to its customers through available communication options / channels for complying with the requirement of periodic updation of KYC.

Prior to the due date of periodic updation of KYC, the RE shall give at least three advance intimations, including at least one intimation by letter, at appropriate intervals to its customers through available communication options/ channels for complying with the requirement of periodic updation of KYC.

arguments.query: Before the due date for periodic updation of KYC, the Bank shall send the customer at least three advance intimations through the available communication channels.

rationale: The clause requires approval from the 'Branch Manager' to continue a relationship with a customer who becomes a PEP, whereas the RBI Directions mandate that 'senior management's approval' must be obtained.

evidence.quote: in the event of an existing customer or the beneficial owner of an existing account subsequently becoming a PEP, the bank obtains the senior management's approval to continue the business relationship;

arguments.query: Where an existing customer, or the beneficial owner of an existing account, subsequently becomes a politically exposed person, the business relationship may continue with the approval of the Branch Manager.

rationale: The clause requires preserving transaction records for ten years and identification records for five years after the relationship ends, which meets and exceeds the RBI's minimum requirement of five years for both categories of records.

evidence.quote: (1) maintain all necessary records of transactions between the bank and the customer, both domestic and international, for at least five years from the date of transaction; (2) preserve the records pertaining to the identification of the customers and their addresses, obtained while opening the account and during the course of business relationship, for at least five years after the business relationship has ended;

arguments.query: Records of transactions shall be preserved for at least ten years from the date of the transaction, and records of customer identification and address for at least five years after the business relationship has ended.

rationale: The clause states that KYC records shall be uploaded within 30 days, whereas the applicable RBI Directions require upload within 10 days of the commencement of the account-based relationship.

evidence.quote: In terms of provision of Rule 9(1A) of the PML Rules, the bank shall capture customer's KYC records and upload onto CKYCR within 10 days of commencement of an account-based relationship with the customer.

arguments.query: The KYC records of new customers shall be uploaded to the Central KYC Records Registry within 30 days of the commencement of the account-based relationship.

rationale: The provided passages from the RBI (Commercial Banks - Know Your Customer) Directions, 2025, mandate ongoing due diligence and periodic KYC updation based on risk categories (2, 8, or 10 years), but they do not contain specific provisions requiring screening against 'adverse media sources' at onboarding or at specific annual intervals. evidence.quote: The bank shall undertake ongoing due diligence of customers to ensure that their transactions are consistent with their knowledge about the customers, customers' business and risk profile, the source of funds / wealth.

arguments.query: All customers shall be screened against adverse media sources at onboarding and at least once a year thereafter.

rationale: The clause specifies the internal schedule for the Compliance Department's coordination meetings, which is an internal administrative matter not governed by the provided RBI notifications regarding DAY-NRLM, Lead Bank Scheme, or DAY-NULM.

arguments.query: The Compliance Department shall hold its weekly coordination meeting every Monday at 10 a.m.

rationale: The clause correctly mandates seeking OTP consent after 30 days of inactivity, but it omits the mandatory requirement to close the credit card account within seven working days if no consent is received.

evidence.quote: If no consent is received for activating the card, card-issuers shall close the credit card account without any cost to the customer within seven working days from date of seeking confirmation from the customer.

arguments.query: Where a credit card has not been activated by the customer within 30 days of issue, the Bank shall seek One Time Password based consent from the cardholder for activating it.

rationale: The clause specifies a penalty of Rs. 500 per 'working day' of delay, whereas the governing RBI Directions mandate a penalty of ₹500 per 'calendar day' of delay, which is a stricter requirement that the bank's policy fails to meet.

evidence.quote: Failure on the part of the card-issuers to complete the process of closure within seven working days shall result in a penalty of ₹500 per calendar day of delay payable to the cardholder, till the closure of the account provided there is no outstanding in the account.

arguments.query: A request to close a credit card shall be completed within seven working days, subject to payment of all dues; for any delay, the Bank shall pay the cardholder Rs. 500 for each working day of delay.

rationale: The clause correctly states the three-day threshold for reporting and levying charges but omits the mandatory requirement to issue a seven-day notice to the cardholder before reporting default status to Credit Information Companies, as well as the specific computation basis for days past due.

evidence.quote: Card-issuers shall report a credit card account as 'past due' to credit information companies (CICs) or levy penal charges, viz. late payment charges and other related charges, if any, only when a credit card account remains 'past due' for more than three days. The number of 'days past due' and late payment charges shall, however, be computed from the payment due date mentioned in the credit card statement, as specified under the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Asset Classification, Provisioning and Income Recognition) Directions, 2026 amended from time to time. Late payment charges and other related charges shall be levied, only on the outstanding amount after the due date, and not on the total amount due.

Before reporting default status of a credit cardholder to a Credit Information Company, the card-issuers shall ensure that they adhere to a procedure, duly approved by their Board, including issuing of a seven-day notice period to such cardholder about the intention to report him/her as defaulter to the Credit Information Company.

arguments.query: A credit card account shall be reported as past due to credit information companies, and late payment charges levied, only when the account remains past due for more than three days.

rationale: The clause requires explicit prior consent for dispatching renewed credit cards, which is stricter than and fully satisfies the RBI requirement to provide the cardholder an option to decline the renewal before dispatch.

arguments.query: Renewed credit cards shall be dispatched only after obtaining the cardholder's explicit prior consent.

rationale: The clause describes an internal operational procedure for closing recurring deposit accounts due to missed instalments, which is a matter of internal bank policy and contract management not governed by specific RBI notifications regarding interest rates, definitions, or responsible business conduct provided in the context.

arguments.query: Recurring deposit accounts with three consecutive missed monthly instalments shall be closed and the balance transferred to the depositor's savings account.

rationale: The clause accurately reflects the mandatory requirement in the RBI Directions that unclaimed proceeds of a matured term deposit must earn interest at the lower of the savings account rate or the contracted rate on the matured deposit.
